title: The Generation of Participation in Democracy
text:
Public Benefit Mission. The Generation of Participation in Democracy (GPD) is a tax-exempt 501(c)(3) public charity and non-governmental organization.
We put education and research into action to help communities enhance their own autonomy, on their own, and accelerate capacity building.
If you would like to support us, please consider supporting our 2027 educational program by helping send laptops and instructors to Indigenous students in Brazil!



Founding leaders Izabela Rezende and Matthew Turner (far right, middle right) with colleagues Laís Albuquerque and Prof. Simone Simionatto (far left, middle left) at the Universidade Federal da Grande Dourados on August 25, 2026.


 GPD IRS Employer Identification Number (EIN): 41-4992916.

Look up our IRS registration with this IRS search tool.




Our Research In Action accelerator program helps founders launch nonprofit research institutes that put actionable insight first, with rigor a close but distinct second.
Prospective accelerator participants must first demonstrate how their institute will spark self-sustaining capacity building that can continue indefinitely, even if the institute and community part ways.


Our Flagship Institute, Instituto Dourados, develops and deploys public health education and monitoring systems in collaboration with Indigenous communities, integrating epidemiology, social science, and multilingual knowledge sharing.



You too could one day build an institution like Instituto Dourados by participating in the program. We review proposals on a rolling basis, depending on interest. Please contact GPD leadership to inquire about your idea.

President & CEO, Dr. Matthew A. Turner
Vice President & Director of Instituto Dourados, Izabela Mauricio de Rezende





Our Future Shaper’s Curriculum is being developed in partnership with the Guateka Academy Secondary School in the Dourados Indigenous Reservation in the state of Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil, facilitated by Instituto Dourados.



Group photo with students, teachers, and visiting family at the Guateka Academy after Instituto Dourados’ workshop there, August 26, 2026.


The curriculum teaches essentials from philosophy, mathematics, programming, efficient computing, social science, leadership and project management skills for current and future future shapers worldwide. Business, policy making, government, and even just daily life have become complex without precedent. The future’s most effective leaders will boast a much deeper expertise across a much broader collection of subjects than is expected of anyone today.
Those completing the course will be able to build new community-strengthening technologies, such as multi-channel emergency alert and community notification systems, which one community leader suggested as a student project.
We have also brainstormed AI-enabled edge devices that could run on solar energy. These devices could run local, highly-specialized, and therefore highly-efficient, translation devices with a camera, a speaker, and a microphone, so the user could interact with it using their voice to understand their information, and no data need ever to travel to the global Internet, and little personal health data need be exposed at all.
Many community members cannot read and do not know Portuguese, only their Indigenous home language. Community leaders have told us that AI-generated audio and video aids that adapt in real-time to user questions and concerns could be life-changing for Indigenous peoples facing scary healthcare emergencies, surgeries, and other healthcare events.
No digitization of languages spoken on the Reservation are available. Current and future students could help design and perform the initial supervised learning stage providing expert instruction to the AI system to seed the model.



Our approach to boosting democratic participation is to raise the global Sustainability VIBE. That is, we create tools and systems to support Vibrant Institutions that ensure everyone’s Basic needs are met. Only when basic needs are met can people be expected contribute to Environmental protection. Future generations need a healthy environment for a good life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness, free from excessive risk and uncertainty.



The Sustainability VIBE in layers, with dependency flowing bottom-up.





Meaningful democratic participation requires transparency. GPD operates under a principle of radical transparency for financial decisions and governance.
To meet our board of directors or review our organizing documents and other accountability information, please visit our Governance page.
Inquiries: transparency@gpd.network
Written by Matthew A. Turner © 2026 The Generation of Participation in Democracy

title: Giving
text:
Support the Generation of Participation in Democracy
Your support enables the development of sustainable, participatory institutions across the Americas. Currently, 100% of contributions go to fund research, field programs, and infrastructure through our Flagship Institute, Instituto Dourados. Once we can fund the first two years of operation of Instituto Dourados we may consider expanding GPD’s institutional portfolio, allocating resources beyond just Instituto Dourados.
Opportunities to support other GPD Américas organizations will be announced as they become available.
Written by Matthew A. Turner © 2026 The Generation of Participation in Democracy

text:

Location: 3318 Line Dr., Merced, CA 95348
Present: Matthew Turner
footer.html

title: GPD Network Shared Governance Establishment
text:
Call to Order
Matthew Turner called the meeting to order for the purpose of establishing the initial governance structure of the GPD Network and recording corresponding governance actions for the organizations it presently serves.

title: GPD Network Shared Governance Establishment
text:
GPD Network Resolution
It is hereby resolved that the GPD Network shall serve as the shared leadership community for its affiliated organizations.
During the initial phase of development, the GPD Network hereby establishes a three-member leadership task force drawn from its Board to actively guide the managed co-evolution of its affiliated organizations.
This task force shall serve as the Board of Directors of Generation of Participation in Democracy (GPD) and provide strategic governance for SubtleTea Solutions (STS), consistent with the governing documents and legal status of each organization.
The task force is constituted as a temporary structure to coordinate alignment, learning, and execution across entities, and shall be adjusted, expanded, or dissolved as needed once the mission of this phase is complete, with planning for the next phase expected to begin as the shape of the solution becomes clear.
The resolution was adopted.

title: GPD Network Shared Governance Establishment
text:
GPD Network Resolution: Financial Separation
The Board recognizes the importance of maintaining appropriate financial separation between its affiliated organizations.
During the initial phase of development, the Board shall establish policies governing financial interactions between Generation of Participation in Democracy (GPD) and SubtleTea Solutions (STS) to ensure transparency, legal compliance, mission alignment, and appropriate organizational independence.
Until such policies are adopted, all financial interactions between affiliated organizations shall be undertaken cautiously and documented in a manner consistent with these principles.
The resolution was adopted.

title: GPD Network Shared Governance Establishment
section: GPD Network Resolution: Appointment of Secretary
text:
GPD Network Resolution: Appointment of Secretary
Matthew Turner appointed Dr. Izabela Mauricio de Rezende to serve as Secretary of the Board of Directors of the GPD Network, effective immediately, to serve until her resignation, removal, or the appointment of a successor.
The resolution was adopted.

title: GPD Network Shared Governance Establishment
text:
GPD Board Resolution
The meeting further records that the initial members of the GPD Network Board shall serve as the Board of Directors of Generation of Participation in Democracy (GPD), consistent with the corporation’s governing documents.
The resolution was adopted.

title: GPD Network Shared Governance Establishment
text:
STS Governance Resolution
As sole owner of SubtleTea Solutions (STS), Matthew Turner confirmed that, during the organization’s initial phase of development, STS shall receive strategic governance from the members of the GPD Network Board.
The resolution was adopted.

title: GPD Network Shared Governance Establishment
text:
Adjournment
There being no further business, the meeting was adjourned.

title: GPD Network Shared Governance Establishment
text:
Approval
The above resolutions are hereby approved and adopted.

Matthew Turner

Date: July 1, 2026

title: Joshua Rueckheim Invited to Join Leadership Team
text:
Call to Order
Dr. Turner, Chair, called the meeting to order and prepared these minutes, which were approved by Dr. Rezende via email.

title: Joshua Rueckheim Invited to Join Leadership Team
section: GPD Network Resolution: Invitation to Join the Board
text:
GPD Network Resolution: Invitation to Join the Board
The Board considered the need for additional financial and operational leadership during the initial phase of development.
Upon motion duly made and seconded, the Board unanimously resolved to invite Joshua Rueckheim to join the Leadership Team as Treasurer and sit on the GPD Network Board of Directors (Mr. Rueckheim’s LinkedIn Profile).
Upon accepting this invitation, Joshua Rueckheim shall be appointed Treasurer of the GPD Network, effective immediately, This shall be effective immediately. Mr. Rueckheim shall serve until his resignation, removal, or the appointment of a successor.
The Treasurer shall assist the Board in developing financial policies, promoting transparency, supporting compliance, and strengthening the long-term stewardship of the Community and its affiliated organizations.
The Board further resolved that, upon accepting the invitation, Mr. Rueckheim shall also become a member of the Board of Directors of Generation of Participation in Democracy (GPD), consistent with the corporation’s governing documents and the shared governance structure established in Meeting #1. Mr. Rueckheim has extensive experience in nonprofit accounting and implementing controls in high-stakes corporate settings.
Matthew Turner, as sole owner of SubtleTea Solutions (STS), further confirmed that, upon accepting the invitation, Joshua Rueckheim shall participate in the strategic governance of STS through his service on the GPD Network leadership task force.
The resolution was adopted unanimously.

title: Governance
text:
Leadership

President and CEO Matthew A. Turner, PhD

Dr. Matt Turner is the founder, president, and CEO of the Generation of Participation in Democracy. He helped co-found Instituto Dourados led by Dr. Rezende, and in partnership with our Indigenous partners. Dr. Turner leads the group effort to develop the Future Shaper’s Curriculum so that it meets our partner students’ needs, fits their interests, and is well-matched to their current capacities to avoid boredom or discouragement.
Dr. Turner leads several GPD initiatives as CEO. He leads the recruitment, founding, and development of new GPD institutes who will put GPD research into action using tools from the Future Shaper toolkit. He provides support to GPD institutes on how to organize and grow their organizations, and teaching support for the Future Shaper’s Curriculum in the classroom or community.
He also leads software development for GPD, creating new and consolidating several existing open source software projects under the common banner of the Sustained Inference brand. Sustained Inference unites GPD’s open software products with computers and other products developed and sold by by Dr. Turner’s company, SubtleTea Solutions.
Dr. Turner’s website


Vice President and Chief Accountability Officer Izabela Mauricio de Rezende, PhD

Dr. Iza Rezende is co-founder, Vice President, and the Chief Accountability Officer of the Generation of Participation in Democracy.
Dr. Rezende leads research and academic initiatives at GPD to deepen our impact across sectors and multiply our impact over time through intentional, clever, and humane cultural accumulation. She is the Founder and Director of GPD’s Flagship Institute, Instituto Dourados.
As Chief Accountability Officer, Dr. Rezende confirms, and corrects if necessary, GPD projects and plans so that they truly serve historically marginalized folks first and foremost, and promote the greater good overall.
Dr. Rezende is a virologist and Research Scientist at the Stanford University School of Medicine, leading interdisciplinary studies on infectious disease epidemiology and virus evolution. Her work bridges real-time genetic identification of what is making people sick with public health intervention strategy design to better protect vulnerable populations.
Dr. Rezende received her PhD in Microbiology and Virology from the Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais, and a MS in Infectious Diseases and BS in Biology from the Universidade Federal de Juiz de Fora in the state of Minas Gerais, Brazil.
Dr. Rezende on LinkedIn


Treasurer Joshua Rueckheim, MBA

Joshua Rueckheim oversees book keeping, develops controls and ensures enforcement, and assists with structuring and executing forecasts and other business processes. Mr. Rueckheim applies his decades of expertise in business management to ensure the financial integrity of the GPD Network’s organizations.
Mr. Rueckheim is currently Finance Director for the Philadelphia Hospitality Investment Levy and for Alta Management Services. Before joining Alta, Mr. Rueckheim worked for Mariott International for 10 years in various finance and accounting roles.
